ca_bee_rock_griffith_park.blurb: Bee Rock is a hive-shaped outcrop inside Griffith Park in Los Angeles, at the edge of the Santa Monica Mountains. Its south-southeast face, roughly 40 to 90 feet tall, carries about fifteen bolted sport routes. The grades run steep and fairly hard: one easy line, then a solid spread through 5.10, 5.11 and 5.12, so it suits climbers already comfortable on sustained sport. In winter the face soaks up sun for most of the day, which makes cool or overcast days the better pick; later in spring and early summer it slips into shade by mid to late afternoon. Some holds are loose, so wear a helmet. The way in is a hike up a fire road and a rocky ravine trail.

ca_lost_horse_wall_right_side.blurb: The right side of Lost Horse Wall is a west-facing, multi-pitch trad cliff in Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,100 feet, with routes reaching roughly 300 feet. All fifteen climbs here are trad. They begin with one easy fifth-class line, add a few at 5.7 and 5.8, and gather most heavily at 5.10, with a pair of 5.11s at the top end, so moderate parties and stronger leaders both find something. The wall gets morning shade and afternoon sun, and it is open to the wind, so blustery days and hot midday hours are best avoided. A worn trail along the base leads to the routes.
ca_lost_horse_wall_right_side.approach: A well-worn trail leaves Lost Horse Road and follows the base of the wall; allow roughly 5 to 15 minutes.

ca_eagle_lake_buttress.blurb: Eagle Lake Buttress is a tower at the south end of a high ridge, about a mile west of Eagle Lake and above Emerald Bay on Lake Tahoe's west shore, within the Eagle Creek Canyon climbing area. Most of its fifteen climbs are alpine-style multi-pitch routes, with a couple of trad lines. They range from a fourth-class scramble through 5.6 to 5.8 lines up to several at 5.9 and 5.10, so there is an easy way up and harder options on the other faces. The easiest line is split into short pitches and ends on a flat, table-like summit with views over the lake. Plan on a long hike in, around an hour and a half from the Emerald Bay lot.

ca_exploding_energy_boulder.blurb: Exploding Energy Boulder is one of the satellite areas at Promontory, a big overhanging sandstone sea cliff beside Highway 101 in Del Norte County, south of Crescent City. The routes face the Pacific. This boulder holds fifteen climbs, nearly all of them bolted sport, with one top-rope and one trad line. The grades cover two easy 5.7s and a 5.9, a good block of 5.10 through 5.12, and a single 5.13, so it works for warm-ups as well as hard projects. Routes are short and the walk to the boulder involves a scramble to the left before you reach the main wall.

ca_m_taboo_area.blurb: On Riverside Quarry's west face, Taboo Area occupies the right-hand part in California's Inland Empire, between The Alcove and The Shield. An arching, steep corner system is the landmark. Of its fifteen routes, fourteen are bolted sport and one is trad. The grades begin with a single 5.10, then pile up in 5.11 and especially 5.12, with two 5.13s, so this is a place for strong climbers rather than beginners. The steep wall offers little shade at midday and summer afternoons run hot, so cooler months or early and late sessions are the better plan. The walk from the car is short.

ca_gopher_s_den.blurb: Gopher's Den is a small bouldering area in the Eastern Sierra near Lone Pine, in the Horseshoe Meadows country, at roughly 11,300 feet. You reach it on foot along the Cottonwood Lakes Trail, about 3.7 miles to the fourth and fifth lakes, with the boulders on the right of the trail. Its fifteen problems run from very easy to V3, with most at V0 and V1, and many see little traffic, so bring a brush to clean holds. It is a pretty place to camp among the boulders and draws long-distance hikers who want a few problems.

ca_egg_the.blurb: The Egg is a free-standing conglomerate formation at the canyon mouth of Texas Canyon, in the Angeles National Forest high desert between Santa Clarita and Agua Dulce. It stands roughly 80 to 120 feet tall and overhangs on every side near the top. Most of its fifteen routes are bolted sport, with a couple of trad and top-rope lines. Grades begin with one easy 5.5 and a 5.8, then bunch up with seven at 5.10, three at 5.11 and three at 5.12, a good fit for mid-grade climbers. Most lines sit on the rounded south buttress. The rock can be loose and gritty until traffic cleans it.
